g.title: app/client.py — runs the ledger in the reasoner's process and calls create_decision, the operation the HTTP route runs.
app/client.py — POST /api/v1/decisions with the reasoner's key in X-DecisionLedger-Key.

app/api/models.py — the decision's outcome (the resolved entity_id and entity_type, the bypass rule and whether it held, the registration_version, every gate's status, the latency breakdown), not its full record; the bundle is at GET /api/v1/decisions/{decision_id}.

text.tspan: bypass rule that holds, or asks for a gate

g.title: The reasoner's assembler. core.submission.matching_bypass_rule returns the strictest registered bypass rule that holds: the submission records that rule's action and cites it (mode record); when none holds it asks for a gate (mode gate). ATO's rules are allow-band (label_value < 0.20, ALLOW) and block-band (label_value > 0.95, BLOCK).
Any failure raises SubmissionContractError (a 422 problem) before a gate runs; nothing is persisted.
IdentityService.identify, under a 50 ms default budget. Any failure records the passthrough subject, unresolved, with the reason; a decision is never refused over its identity.

Gate-level tiers per gate output, then the decision-level rules and the combinator over ALLOW < CHALLENGE < HOLD < BLOCK. A failing gate fails closed (HOLD). The bypass checks are snapshotted into the bundle.
The domain's raw event. It crosses to the ledger only as opaque raw_event JSON.
Every feature the model consumed; it travels as reasoner_context.feature_set, which bypass rules and replay read.
ATO's XGBoost risk score and top signals; it travels as reasoner_context.label_value and attribution.
